subject: Keychain integrity, rotation logs & transport manifest — SOC2 appendix
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Kuznetsov <elena.k@acme-finance.com>, security@acme-finance.com
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Keychain integrity, rotation logs & transport manifest — SOC2 appendix

Hi Elena / Acme security team,

Per our SOC 2 appendix conversation, attaching the minimal artifact set you requested to demonstrate key rotation and secure transport for tenant KEKs. This thread will track: the rotation manifest, a transport log sample, and a short integrity statement for our keychain process.

Attached in this initial drop:
- rotation_manifest_20270515.csv (summary of recent KEK rotations: tz, operator, origin host, wrapping key id)
- transport_log_sample_20270516.txt (redacted SFTP push log showing checksums)
- kms_keychain_integrity_statement.pdf (one-page summary of procedure and control owners)

Ask: please confirm the artifact names are sufficient for your SOC 2 auditor (or tell us what additional sampling you need). If acceptable, we can push the full sample set to your secure SFTP location and provide a signed hash manifest.

High-level notes:
- All rotations for customer-managed KEKs are orchestrated via the rotation service (runbook v2.1) and require two operators for production pushes.
- Transport uses SFTP with server-side key pinning; logs are retained for 90 days per our retention policy.
- Manifest rows are checksumed and signed with our platform signing key; we can provide a time-stamped signature if the auditor prefers.

Next steps we propose:
1) Confirm artifact acceptance.
2) We push the full sample set to sftp://s-secure.acme-finance.com/incoming/redwood/keyproofs/.
3) Post-push, we provide signed SHA256 manifest and a short chain-of-custody note.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

---
Attachment stubs: rotation_manifest_20270515.csv (CSV, 24 rows), transport_log_sample_20270516.txt (TXT, redacted), kms_keychain_integrity_statement.pdf (PDF, 1 page)
From: Elena Kuznetsov <elena.k@acme-finance.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-finance.com, auditops@acme-finance.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Keychain integrity, rotation logs & transport manifest — SOC2 appendix

Jordan — thanks for the quick response and the initial artifacts. A couple of clarifications from the Acme audit team: 

1) For the rotation manifest, we need an additional column indicating the wrapping key fingerprint used for each KEK rotation event (for cross-checking with our supplier inventory).
2) For the transport logs, can you provide a short note on how logs are protected at rest on your side (encryption-at-rest details + who/what can access raw logs)?
3) We would prefer the signed SHA256 manifest be timestamped with an RFC 3339 timestamp and PGP-signed for chain-of-custody.

If you can get a revised CSV and an access-control note to us by end of day Wednesday (our time), we can accept the sample and forward it to the external auditor. Also confirm whether the SFTP account will be created by Acme or by Redwood.

Best,
Elena
Elena Kuznetsov
Director, Information Security — Acme Finance
elena.k@acme-finance.com
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Kuznetsov <elena.k@acme-finance.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Keychain integrity, rotation logs & transport manifest — SOC2 appendix

Elena / team — replying with the technical details you requested and an updated manifest attached.

What we changed / added: 
- rotation_manifest_20270515.csv (new column: wrapping_key_fingerprint, values are SHA256 of wrapping key public material)
- transport_log_sample_20270516.txt (unchanged; added an explanatory header line in the SFTP sample)
- kms_keychain_integrity_statement.pdf now includes a short section on log encryption + access matrix

Log protection summary (short):
- Logs are written to an encrypted object store (AES-256-GCM) with per-bucket CMKs managed in our KMS.
- Access to raw logs requires a role-bound service account and is audited via immutable audit records (joined with our SIEM).
- Rotating KMS keys that protect logs is part of our quarterly rotation schedule; those rotations are logged in the same manifest system (and you can sample them on request).

Transport / SFTP: 
- We support two onboarding models: (A) Acme creates a dedicated SFTP account on your side and provides creds; (B) Redwood uploads to an Acme-managed SFTP endpoint (we prefer option A for separation of duties).
- When we push artifacts, we include a PGP-signed SHA256 manifest and an RFC 3339 timestamp in the manifest header.

Attached: rotation_manifest_20270515_v2.csv, transport_log_sample_20270516.txt, kms_keychain_integrity_statement.pdf

Jonas has also added a single-sentence operator attestation in the footer of the manifest.

—
Irene Choi
Mgr, Cryptography & Key Ops, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Kuznetsov <elena.k@acme-finance.com>, security@acme-finance.com
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Keychain integrity, rotation logs & transport manifest — SOC2 appendix

Elena — thank you, and noted. Confirming next steps: 

- We will publish rotation_manifest_20270515_v2.csv (includes wrapping_key_fingerprint and operator attestation) and the signed manifest to your SFTP location if Acme creates the account (preferred).
- If Acme prefers Redwood to push, we will require an Acme-managed ingress endpoint and a short MOU confirming transfer responsibilities.
- Attached PDFs include the updated integrity statement and the operator attestation.

Deliverables timeline:
- By EOD Friday (your time) — PGP-signed SHA256 manifest uploaded to sftp://s-secure.acme-finance.com/incoming/redwood/keyproofs/ (pending account).
- Within 48 hours after upload — provide a short chain-of-custody note signed by the operator (Jonas).

Please advise which onboarding model you prefer and we will proceed.

Thanks again — we want to keep the auditor's sampling window small and make this as self-contained as possible.

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]
